The three Wiki pages read in this batch do not independently verify them, so they are not marked SUPPORTED by this batch.
The Hiderion short page independently supports only the theoretical-empire distinction; the Township page does not establish those detailed criticisms.

rationale.campaign_length: Y86 has 61 direct missions; Y00 has a further 124 related missions, inherited by stage and not directly additive.
rationale.colonization: The missions reach into colonisation of the Ringlet Isles, but the campaign’s main axis remains the integration of existing Halessi states.
rationale.complexity: Representation, culture groups, republican tradition, construction thresholds, powerful neighbours, and a long mission line must be handled in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: Conquest, elven leadership, and historical distrust create controversy, but the main line is not a horror or destruction narrative.
rationale.difficulty: The small-country opening and complex formation thresholds raise the difficulty; strength increases after the Empire is formed.
rationale.diplomacy: Early relations with local lords and allies, followed by multi-cultural representation and subject arrangements, require political coordination.
rationale.early_pressure: In 1444 the small township must secure survival and an initial unification window between stronger powers.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The current missions are defined by representation, military organisation, and unification; magic and artifice are not the main axis.
rationale.narrative_density: Hiderion’s origins, township figures, the parliamentary ideal, imperial formation, and the succession branch form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: The citadel, new capital, ports, and transport construction matter, but they serve expansion across regions.
rationale.trade_economy: Industry, ports, porcelain, and transport networks are prominent, but none is the sole core mechanic.
rationale.warfare: The campaign extends from township unification to military and political integration across multiple Halessi regions, requiring sustained warfare.

identity.appearance: A 1444 Sikai Township republic ruled by the Sunrise Elf Hiderion Tonanzuir.

successors.relationship: Formed by completing Y86’s exclusive missions and firing azkare.42; retains the origin missions and continues into the imperial stage.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and the ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. description.text:
The elf Hiderion was born an unknown peasant, his family name coming from Lord Tonan Prakuong, who took notice of his talents and informally adopted him. For two human generations he served as a valued advisor and retainer of the Azkare lords, being granted lordship for his loyal service to the township.

For a peasant to rise to become the most powerful man in the land serves as an inspiration to the masses of Azkare, who work tirelessly in hopes of replicating his meteoric rise to power.

description.text: At the center of Azkare is the Citadel of the Dawn, a fortress built by the Phoenix Empire to overlook the trade routes of the upper Telebei as it passes through the area. The city was built around this bastion, which has been maintained as the palace of our lords, its soaring walls still protecting Azkare and allowing a thriving market to be established just outside of it.

description.text: Khanvuphaim is a unique fabric only found in Azkare, woven from feathers by master artisans using an art that has been passed down for generations. Its softness and weightlessness make it a highly prized commodity in Thidinkai and beyond.

description.text: The sun elves that manned the citadel of Azkare utilized a style of cavalry far different from the usual in these lands, cladding their steeds in thick armor and wielding long steel lances. The horsemen of the Phoenix Empire survive in Haless in the form of the Shining Lancers of Azkare, fully armored and decorated with Khanvuphaim garments, acting as our elite cavalry units.

description.text: Being on the border of the Xianjie, we receive many exiles from the mysterious land to our city. They reside in the Nakhriban, and earn a living by teaching our people their arts, greatly improving the quality of our armed forces.
description.text_en: Being on the border of the Xianjie, we receive many exiles from the mysterious land to our city. They reside in the Nakhriban, and earn a living by teaching our people their arts, greatly improving the quality of our armed forces.

description.text:
As the Nakhriban grows, more and more of our people learn their formerly secret arts. The most ardent and adept students are found amongst the elves of the city, who have used their long lives to develop an entirely new school, the School of the Phoenix, to be taught to every member of our armies.

By combining the martial prowess of the Xianjie monks with the discipline of the elves, our brave soldiers have become a force to be reckoned with, unwavering in their demeanor and relentless in their assault.

description.text:
Scattered throughout the lands of Haless lie those elves left behind by the cataclysmic fall of the Phoenix Empire. Hunted out of vengeance and distrusted by most, they scrape by as best they can, living in squalor for centuries until they finally pass from this world. For most this seems a fitting punishment for the invaders and oppressors of this land, though others see a path for redemption. The great lord Hiderion ruled over his human subjects not as a tyrant but as their righteous guardian, a true servant of the people and a paragon of the ideals set by Jaerel.

For the elves of Haless to thrive in this land, they must do so as equals of those that have called this land home for millennia, united in harmony under an serene empire, built on the virtues Hiderion lived by. We must not rule Haless as conquerors, nor as her "saviors". We must rule as her guardians, protectors of the peace and sentinels against those that would seek to exploit her.

description.text:
While Harimar managed to conquer the Rahenraj and Yanshen, he and his descendants never had the means nor desire to conquer the rest of Haless proper. Jaher, however, did not have those limitations. By the time of Jaher's death in 1127, the Phoenix Empire stretched from Bulwar to Tianlou to Arawkelin, and even the stalwart kingdoms of the Sikai were in talks of joining the empire as a peaceful partner.

With the resurgence of the Phoenix Empire in Haless, it is by right that Haless be united under a single benevolent entity once again.

description.text: Meaning 'noblesse oblige' or 'nobility obliges', this phrase hearkens back to the sun elven attitudes as benevolent and impartial rulers of the land. Because of their duty to rule and to protect, the sun elven people must be held to higher accountabilities and expectations. They must be a good force in the world; kind and generous, patient with even those that disobey, and ultimately, be the embodiment of Surael in the world.

description.text:
Formed by an elite cadre of Transmutative Path monks and Sikai warriors, the Jaerelic Legions became the modern version of Jaher's Phoenix Legions with one core difference: they accepted and heavily utilized non-elves. While this style was also adopted by the Jaddari, the legions of the Sunrise Empire focused on the collective values of the Halessi peoples and incorporated the ritualistic gestures of the Transmutative Path in their drilling techniques, making them a fierce opponent in the field.

Their most famous technique was the 'Burning Dragon Technique', which was essentially a fire-and-advance tactic done at an incredibly fast pace, allowing an entire regiment to continuously fire on the enemy immediately prior to entering into melee range.

description.text:
Unlike his father, who dreamed only of conquest, and his sister, who dreamed of elven supremacy, Jaerel dreamed of a world united as one - regardless of race, creed or belief, which he espoused to a point in making the love of his life, the harimari princess Tataka, his primary wife. Unfortunately, Jaerel's stance was only seen as a failure to choose a side, which saw many of his allies abandon him.

Times have changed, however, and as the world is led by the scions of Anbennar, a realm created to bring peace and equality, perhaps Haless is now ready to see that All Are Equals Beneath the Rising Sun.

description.text:
Rezan Zimhar. The Alliance of the Sun. Found and translated by scholars in the 19th century from a lost part of Jaerel's will, the Rezan Zimhar was a plan to essentially federalize the disparate and diverse cultures and religions of Haless into a united state which granted them great amounts of autonomy and privileges, all under an impartial sun elven central court. Assumed to be greatly inspired by events surrounding the collapse of Jaerel's empire-building efforts, he had hoped to present this proposal at Sarisung shortly before he was assassinated.

Now that the Sunrise Empire shines ones again, perhaps Jaerel's ambition can now be realized.

description.text:
The sun elves brought with them arcane magic, a form of magic that was mastered through study and learning. Before that, most magic-users in Haless either utilized chi (their spiritual energy) or were outcasts studying rough forms of arcane, druidic, or other magics in the fringes of Halessi society.

The Monks of the Weaving Palm were a collection of sun elven magi, high philosophers and Transmutative Path monks who apparently spent a hundred days and nights debating on the nature of spirits and magic in the High Temple of Tianlou.

There, they developed a concept of magic that was described as 'the weave', something that one must connect with on a spiritual basis to master, not just through study. While the concept of 'the weave' never reached wide-spread popularity, the Monks of the Weaving Palm proved incredibly deadly in battle, evoking arcane spells through movements and gestures akin to chi and cultivation practices, using nothing but their internal energies - the arcane 'weave' in the air - rather than spell reagents and components.

description.text: A common saying within the Sunrise Empire, possibly originating from ancient Yan proverbs, "We All Lift Together" was a slogan used during the industrialization initiatives of the Age of Artificery when many factories, funded by artificers and magnates, were created across Haless. It is said that the unity of the Sunrise Empire saw that every man, woman and child, regardless of race, had a role in lifting up the empire - or in a factory's case, worked as one in an assembly line.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who only want rapid conquest, dislike representation and construction prerequisites, or do not want to manage powerful-neighbour pressure and a long mission chain.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Stabilise a small country in Thidinkai, unite the townships, and establish parliament; then advance conquest, cultural representation, a new capital, and port construction in parallel, before managing a larger Halessi integration after forming the Sunrise Empire.
player_overview.overview: You are Azkare, a small township in Thidinkai, Haless, in 1444, ruled by the elven peasant-born Hiderion. Survive between stronger neighbours and unite the townships; then every conquest and accepted region raises the question of how different cultures gain representation in parliament. With the capital, ports, and political institutions prepared, you can form the Sunrise Empire and carry an ideal of multi-cultural rule across Haless. The tension between an elven arbiter and continental conquest never disappears.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy a weak-country long narrative, parliament and culture management, complex imperial construction, and a controversial idealistic route.
signature_features: Cultural representation and parliamentary seats are direct mission and formation thresholds, not mere background.
Hiderion’s rise from peasant to lord connects township unification, personal legitimacy, and the ideal of multi-cultural rule.
A Y86-exclusive event forms Y00 and continues the missions; Hiderion’s death also enables a Sikai succession divergence.
player_overview.tagline: Begin with a township ruled by an elven lord and give Haless’s peoples seats in one parliament.

reasons: Parliamentary representation is directly coupled to conquest and unification
Hiderion’s personal story and the Sunrise ideal run through the long campaign
The Empire continues with missions and a multi-cultural military system
warnings: High pressure from the small-country opening and stronger neighbours
Representation and construction thresholds limit purely military progress
The imperial ideal and elven leadership are not free of contradiction

positive_indicators: Cultural representation enters parliament and mission conditions
A person of peasant origin can achieve political advancement
Public construction such as a new capital, roads, and ports
values.rationale: A multi-cultural representative system, opposition to aristocratic birth monopolies, and public transport construction have clear positive aims; however, the elven arbiter role, boundaries around some outsider cultures and religions, and conquest-based unification reduce restraint. The score does not change because of imperialisation, elven identity, or expansion itself, and does not treat the Wiki’s theoretical Empire as accomplished history.
red_flags: Using war to advance political unification across regions
A power asymmetry between the elven arbiter and equal representation
The ideal state is not unconditionally open to some outsider cultures and religions
